title: SFIA
lead: Skills Framework for the Information Age — a globally recognised competency framework for IT professionals.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: SFIA provides a common language for describing IT skills and competencies. It defines skills across seven levels of responsibility, from following instructions to setting strategy. Organisations use SFIA to define job roles, assess capability gaps, plan development and manage workforce transformation. SFIA is widely used in IT outsourcing contracts to define skill requirements.

sections.heading: ITOM Perspective
sections.body: In ITOM engagements, SFIA is used to design the people dimension of the target operating model — defining roles, skill requirements and development paths. It is particularly relevant in outsourcing transitions and agile transformations where new role profiles are required.

items.desc: 7 categories covering IT practices from strategy to user support.
7 levels from 'Follow' to 'Set Strategy' — defining seniority and autonomy.
Combinations of SFIA skills used to define job descriptions.
Mapping current workforce skills against SFIA to identify gaps.
Using SFIA gaps to design targeted training and career paths.
